original_title: World: Turkish Red Crescent Monthly Activity Bulletin - July 2026
title: World: Turkish Red Crescent Monthly Activity Bulletin - July 2026
original_summary:
Countries: World, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran (Islamic Republic of), Iraq, Lebanon, occupied Palestinian territory, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen
Source: Turkish Red Crescent Society

Please refer to the attached file.

Afghanistan

Afghanistan Social Assistance Activities

Within the scope of Social Assistance Activities in Afghanistan, a total of 622 food parcels consisting of nine essential food items were distributed to vulnerable families and families with orphaned children in the central districts of Maidan Wardak and Kabul provinces, as well as to vulnerable families affected by flooding in Nuristan Province. Through this intervention, assistance was provided to 4,976 beneficiaries.

Bangladesh

Vocational Training Activities

At TRC’s Camp-5 Vocational Training Center, a total of 80 trainees enrolled in the 17th and 18th cohorts are continuing their vocational training programs. Of these, 40 participants are attending the Handicrafts Training Program, while the remaining 40 are enrolled in the Block Printing and Boutique Skills Training Program. The training activities for all beneficiaries are ongoing.

original_title: Iran-Afghanistan - Returns Emergency Response #32 (as of 1 August 2026)
title: Iran-Afghanistan - Returns Emergency Response #32 (as of 1 August 2026)
original_summary:
Countries: Iran (Islamic Republic of), Afghanistan
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

Context

On 20 March 2025, headcount slips for an estimated 2 million Afghans in Iran expired, after which the Government introduced a regularization and return scheme, requiring slip holders to undergo assessments to determine whether they can remain.

Since then, returns have increased significantly. In 2025, more than 1.9 million Afghans returned or were deported from Iran – many not by choice. In 2026, a further 426,700 Afghans have returned. These large-scale returns are placing pressure on basic services, housing and livelihoods in Afghanistan, straining host communities and increasing the risks of instability and onward movement.

At the same time, hostilities across Asia and the Middle East since 28 February 2026 have further compounded the situation. As one of the largest refugee-hosting countries in the region, Iran is facing growing pressure amid rising humanitarian needs, highlighting the need for flexible and sustained support.
